answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying rewards to unpredictable live audits instead of account count. At random moments, like a comet nobody can schedule, each identity must solve a fresh task within minutes, and peers check that the answers differ in substance. One operator running 300 aliases must then do 300 real jobs at once, so the ridge where faking stays cheaper than honest work disappears. Payouts stay locked until several audits pass, leaving a quartz-hard record a farm cannot backdate.
